summary:
AgriGate is a free web app that helps farmers decide what to plant next, using 20 years of NASA POWER climate data for their own field. 

A farmer drops a pin on the map, chooses rainfed or irrigated, enters the crops they grow now, and picks one goal: balance, soil health, saving water, or profit. AgriGate checks 32 crops against local temperature, rainfall, root-zone soil moisture and sunlight. It then suggests a 2–4 season rotation that beats the current plan, shows the expected profit at the farmer’s own prices, and ends with a plain checklist of what to confirm in the field.

The Future Simulator tests that plan in hotter, drier years. A small model trained on the field’s own NASA soil-moisture history warns which months may run short of water and what to change.

AgriGate lets farmers navigate these decisions themselves. Every result comes as a plain verdict, not a technical score: they can try options, see the trade-offs, and adapt their own fields with confidence.
details:
What it does
AgriGate is a free browser app that turns 20 years of NASA POWER data (temperature, rainfall, root-zone soil moisture and sunlight) for one field into planting decisions. A farmer drops a pin on the map, chooses rainfed or irrigated, enters their current crops and picks a goal. Five tabs guide the decision:

  • Rotation Plan: a better 2–4 season rotation, with clear reasons and a field checklist.
  • Crop Suitability: 32 crops ranked by how well they fit the local weather.
  • Profit & Costs: expected profit at the farmer’s own prices.
  • Weather Trends: how the last 5 years differ from the 20-year normal.
  • Future Simulator: how the plan holds up in hotter, drier years. A small model trained on the field’s own soil-moisture history warns which months may run short of water.

Benefits and impact
Advice built on the farmer’s own field, in plain words, on a phone, with no account. AgriGate helps farmers leave risky monoculture, cut fertilizer costs, break pest cycles and prepare for dry seasons. Above all, it lets them navigate these decisions themselves instead of waiting for an expert.

Tools

  • React, Vite and Tailwind CSS, with Recharts for charts and Leaflet for the map.
  • NASA POWER API, FAO GAEZ and FAOSTAT data, Open-Meteo for elevation.
  • Python and Google Colab to explore the data; GitHub and Vercel to share and host the app.
  • AI assistants (Claude) helped with coding and testing.

Creativity
AgriGate turns climate charts into a concrete rotation and a one-line verdict. Its soil-water model learns each field’s own history directly in the browser.

Factors considered

  • Simplicity: no jargon on screen.
  • Honesty: every estimate is labelled, and the app works with a slow connection.
  • Limits of satellite data: a checklist covers what satellites cannot see, such as soil pH, salinity and pests.
